title: Malchus becomes its own face: the world of speech, the separation, and the building of Malchus
overview: Chapter 47 explains how *Malchus* (kingship) becomes a face of its own. *Malchus* is the world of speech, the revealed side opposite the world of thought, and it is taken from the tenth part of each of the ten *sefiros* of *Zeir Anpin*. At first it is attached to *Zeir Anpin*, like Adam and Chava joined together, and the *nesira* (separation) lets it be built into a *partzuf* of its own. The revealed essence of a feeling is the *tzelem* (form), like the picture on a seal stamped into wax; the *demus* (likeness) reflects a thing without being it. Speech turns an inner feeling into a separate *yesh* once it is spoken. *Malchus* begins as a single point under the *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin* and is built up to a full face that stands face to face with it. *Malchus* is also *dal*, poor: it has nothing of its own, only what it receives from *Zeir Anpin*. In the lower worlds it becomes the head and is hidden like the night. Before the separation it was the back that follows the face, without an essence of its own. Learning anything works the same way: first *bittul*, then mastery.

sections.title: Malchus is the world of speech, the revealed side of Atzilus
sections.summary: Malchus is the world of speech, set against thought: the partzuf of Rachel, the revealed world, the lower Ima and the last heh of the Name. Speech is the outward form of what a person first knows inside.

blocks.text: The class has just finished the garment that surrounds *Zeir Anpin* (the small countenance). Now it turns to the building of *Malchus* (kingship), which this chapter and the next few explain. The topic ties to much of the book: *tzimtzum*, *reshimu*, the letters, and the vessels and garments from before. Everything should be connected to it.

*Malchus* of *Atzilus* is the world of speech, as opposed to the world of thought: the *partzuf* of *Rachel*, where *Leah* is thought and *Rachel* is speech. It is the revealed world, the lower *Ima*, and the last *heh* of *Havaya*.

Like mother, like daughter: the upper *heh*, which is *bina*, lends her garments, the five letters that take a different form at the end of a word, to her daughter. These are the five organs of articulation of speech.

Thought first cuts an experience into distinctions, which become letters; those are then represented by distinctions in speech. First you distinguish things in what you know, and only then build a language and symbols to express them in outward words.

blocks.title: An open utterance
blocks.text: An open utterance is one that is revealed: thought is talking to oneself, speech is open for others to hear. "Let there be light" is an open utterance, and "by the word of G-d the heavens were made" shows speech creating something separate. G-d's *malchus* goes into everything and creates it, as is known.

sections.title: Malchus is separated from Zeir Anpin and built into its own face
sections.summary: Malchus starts out attached to the back of Zeir Anpin, like Adam and Chava joined together. After the nesira, the separation, it is built into a partzuf of its own, with its own lights and vessels.

blocks.text: The *nesira* (separation) is known. *Malchus* was once included in *Zeir Anpin*, as Adam and Chava were originally connected, at least as the *Midrash* describes it: two faces attached, until Hashem separated them and made Chava her own person.

blocks.title: From a cry to a language
blocks.text: The *mashal*: a baby crying is simply a natural expression of how he feels. When a person becomes self-aware of what he is doing, it can become its own thing: he can make it a sound in his language, or a custom or practice, and codify it.

This is the same process: first a person is simply creative, making art, and then decides to make certain symbols into a language. That natural self-expression, *Malchus* attached to *Zeir Anpin*, becomes separated and its own thing.

Originally *Malchus* was included in the back, the outer part, of *Zeir Anpin*. Adam found no mate among the animals; when Chava was brought, he said she was "a bone from my bones," taken from man and a part of him.
After the separation, *Malchus* is built into its own *partzuf* with its own lights and vessels. At first it was only an extension of *Zeir Anpin*.
The verse *vayiven Hashem Elokim et ha-tzela* ("Hashem built the rib") is read simply, following Rashi and the *Midrashim*, as the side of *Adam*.

sections.title: Each sefira has its own Malchus: the tenth part, and the revealed yesh
sections.summary: Malchus is taken from the tenth of each of the ten sefiros of Zeir Anpin. Each sefira's Malchus is that sefira made tangible and recognizable, from the first knowing of what a person feels up to speech.

phrases.en: the explanation is known
in the *Zohar* and *Etz Chaim*, in many places
*Malchus* is called the 10th

phrases.he: כי נלקחה מעשיראה דכל עשר ספירות דזעיר אנפין,

phrases.he: דהיינו מבחינת מלכות של כל ספירה דזעיר אנפין

blocks.text: Which body part the side is depends on the translation. The *Midrashim* we hold say they were attached at the back. One opinion says it was like a tail: people used to have one, and Hashem took it off. He can't say for certain what it was.
According to *Kabbalah*, these are different opinions about which way the *yud* should face, back to back or face to back, and they represent different levels of the relationship.
The explanation is known: the *Zohar* and *Etz Chaim* say it in many places.
*Malchus* is called the tenth: it is taken from the tenth of each of the ten *sefiros* of *Zeir Anpin*, separated off to become that *sefira* of *Malchus*.

phrases.he: כמו מבחינת מלכות דחכמה דזעיר אנפין נמשך בחינת חכמה דמלכות,
phrases.en: for example, that the *Malchus* of *chachma* of *Zeir Anpin* becomes the *chachma* of *Malchus*

phrases.he: ומבחינת מלכות דחסד דזעיר אנפין נמשך חסד דמלכות כו',
phrases.en: and the *Malchus* of *chesed* becomes the *chesed* of *Malchus*, etc.

phrases.he: ועל דרך זה נבנו כל עשר ספירות דמלכות
phrases.en: and in this way all the 10 *sefiros* of *Malchus* were constructed

blocks.text: For example, the *Malchus* of *chachma* of *Zeir Anpin* becomes the *chachma* of *Malchus*, and so on.
This is like the earlier idea of *Adam Kadmon*: the *Malchus* of the higher level becomes the *Keser* of the lower, and each *Malchus* of a higher *sefira* becomes the *sefira* below.
The simple idea: when a person speaks, he expresses what he feels, so he must first know what he feels and be conscious of it. Only then can he put it into words.
There are many dimensions to this. In this way all ten *sefiros* of *Malchus* were built.

phrases.he: וביאור בחינת מלכות דט' ספירות דזעיר אנפין ידוע,
phrases.en: so that the idea of the *Malchus* of each of these *sefiros* is known

phrases.en: this is the idea when each *sefira* becomes revealed as a *yesh*, as something tangible so that you can know what it is
for example

when a person has the feeling of love, that it could be hidden, that a person has this innate love, and sometimes it comes out in an open and revealed way where they feel a revealed love for the person, and they want to do a kindness for them

blocks.text: The *Malchus* of each *sefira* is its revelation when it comes out into the open as a *yesh*: something concrete that you can recognize as what it is. That is the *Malchus* of that *sefira*.

Nothing is expressed outward yet. Knowing to yourself what idea you had is the *Malchus* of *chachma*; clarifying it enough to put into words is the *Malchus* of *bina*; and being aware of a desire for kindness and knowing what you want to do is the *Malchus* of *chesed*.
Sometimes feelings are not well defined; people teach children to tell when they are happy, angry or sad. You can have much going on inside without expressing it clearly.
This ties to the *kelim* of *Zeir Anpin*: the *middos* appear as physical sensations, and those changes in the body are how you know what you feel.

blocks.title: Revealed love
blocks.text: For example, a person may have a natural love hidden inside, and sometimes it comes out openly, so he feels a revealed love for someone and wants to do a kindness for him.

sections.title: The revealed essence is a form, a seal and a likeness
sections.summary: What is revealed from a person's inner essence is called a form (tzelem), like the picture on a seal stamped into wax, and his likeness (demus), a reflection that shows the thing without being it. The letters of a seal are themselves engraved to stamp something else.

phrases.he: והנה בחינת ההתגלות הזאת העצמיות נקרא צלם
phrases.en: so when that feeling is revealed within the person's heart, within their consciousness, that's called the essential form
like when you have a seal, if you have a signet ring
so the idea is that you engrave a certain picture into that, and then you can stamp that into wax, but the form, the picture that's on the original thing is like the source of it
or like the form of a person's face
that's the idea of the *kelim* of *Zeir Anpin*

phrases.he: שעל זה אמר איהו וגרמוהי חד,
phrases.en: about that it says, when we're speaking in the *nimshal* about G-d, we say G-d and His organs are one
and like we spoke before, that the *kelim* of *Zeir Anpin* are the idea of a potential limitation
like we explained previously

blocks.text: This revealed feeling is called the essential form, the *tzelem* (image). It is like a seal: you engrave a picture into it and stamp it into wax, but the picture on the original is the source of the stamp.

blocks.title: Thoughts stamped into language
blocks.text: A person stamps his thoughts and feelings into the language he uses. First he must know what he thinks and what he wants to say.

blocks.title: Advice for a writer
blocks.text: Someone who writes was told it matters more to study the subject than to study writing: thoughts to share outweigh good writing with nothing to share. With a clear sense of what you want to say, you can say it.
Studying writing and speaking helps too. Getting clear about what you feel and think is this essential form.
Just as every person has a different face, every person has a different nature, character and way of thinking, spiritually and emotionally. That is called their spiritual *partzuf*.

The forms that express what a person feels, or his body, are the *kelim* of *Zeir Anpin*. About G-d we say "He and His organs are one": the essence of Torah, what is G-dly and holy, and His attributes.

G-d can create something from nothing: that is the *chesed* of *Atzilus*. Hiding that He creates, so we feel independent, is the *gevura* of *Atzilus*. Tanya's *Shaar HaYichud VeHaEmuna* goes through these.
These abilities are one with Him, since He is G-d and does whatever He wants. This is how He reveals Himself within creation: the *kelim* of *Zeir Anpin*.

The *kelim* of *Zeir Anpin* are a potential limitation. G-d is unlimited and can do whatever He wants, and He can choose to reveal Himself in a specific, limited way, as a parent can throw a ball lightly to a child. That is not a real limitation, only an expression of choice. In *Zeir Anpin* the limitation shows that G-d is unlimited.
So it is called only a potential limitation, as explained earlier about the *kelim* of *Zeir Anpin*.

phrases.he: אבל בחינת דמות בנוקבא דזעיר אנפין,
phrases.en: but the idea of the *demus*

phrases.he: שנקרא דמות כבוד יהו״ה דזעיר אנפין
phrases.en: and like it says that on the throne of glory there was the *demus*, the reflection or the likeness of the glory of G-d
as is known
like it says, "Let us make man in our likeness like our form," or "in our form like our likeness"
that *tzelem* is the masculine aspect and *demus* is the feminine aspect

blocks.text: *Tzelem* (image) is masculine and *demus* (likeness) is feminine, as in "Let us make man in our image, like our form."
*Demus* is a likeness: a reflection, or an impression pressed into wax. It is not the thing itself; it reveals something but is not the thing.
The verse says that on the throne of glory was the *demus*, the likeness of G-d's glory, the feminine side of *Zeir Anpin*, as is known.

phrases.en: that G-d engraves letters

phrases.he: שהוא בחינת התגלות להתגלות כאותיות החותם הנחקק בשעוה וכהאי גוונא כו'
phrases.en: and this is the idea that it's a revelation for revelation, like the letters on a signet ring, which are then stamped into wax

blocks.text: This goes back to chapter 10, where G-d engraves letters: *gelef gelifu*, an engraving that is engraved. Why the double expression?
The letters are there for the purpose of making other letters: like a signet ring, whose letters are there so that they can be stamped onto something else.

blocks.title: The printing press
blocks.text: In the olden days a printing press used carved blocks of wood or metal, arranged and locked in place to stamp books. Language is the same: when a person has thoughts and feelings inside, language is just a medium, like clay or a screen you stamp something onto. You use its symbols to represent the idea and carry it to others.

blocks.title: Engraving in crystal
blocks.text: He thinks *Shaarei Orah* gives this *mashal* more fully: a letter engraved into crystal or diamond is hard to read, because there is little contrast. Stamped into something coarser, it gives contrast, and then it can be seen.
The letters are already in *Zeir Anpin*: the power of limitation is hidden in the unlimited, until it is revealed as something separate. That is the general *mashal*.

sections.title: Speech turns a feeling into a yesh of its own
sections.summary: What a person feels inside becomes a separate yesh when he says it. Once spoken, it is out of his hands: others hear it, can misread it, and it stands apart from him. G-d's speech works the same way.

phrases.he: כך בחינת התגלות העצמיות שבמדה שבלב,
phrases.en: and so, too, when a person is expressing how they feel in words, so they have this inner feeling of love for somebody
it's hard to really express what you're feeling in words
comes out and then in the five organs of articulation, the mouth, the tongue, the palate, the throat, the larynx

phrases.he: נעשה בבחינת יש נבדל בפני עצמו,
phrases.en: so then, when you say it, it's now separate from you
and so that is called the something, the real something
as is explained elsewhere at length

blocks.text: The same is true of a feeling in the heart expressed in words: an inner feeling, say of love, is hard to express in words.
You do your best to imprint the feeling into the words. Once it comes out through the five organs of articulation, it is a *yesh* that stands apart: separate, once it is said.
While it is felt, a feeling is private. Once said, others hear it, remember it, are affected by it, and can take it the opposite way from what you meant.
It can be done on purpose: people twist words, the way the media clip a little sound bite, and people get canceled for something they said out of context and things like that.

sensitivity.reason: Names the media as a group that clips sound bites to twist what people said.
sensitivity.publishable: It can be done on purpose: people twist words, clip a little sound bite, and people get canceled for something they said out of context and things like that.

blocks.text: That is the beauty of speech: you can express to someone else what you feel, and once you say it, it is separate from you, a real something.
There is the *yesh* of the *ayin*, the tangible feeling that is *Malchus* of *Zeir Anpin*. Expressed in thought, speech and action, especially speech and action, it becomes a real *yesh*.
It becomes something totally separate, as is explained elsewhere at length.

phrases.he: הבא בגלוי באופן מוגבל, הרי עדיין אחוז ומתאחד בעצם החכמה והחסד כו'

blocks.title: Chachma of chesed in the heart
blocks.text: For example, the *chachma* of *chesed*: an idea of how to help, still inside a person, stays attached to his *etzem*, so it can keep changing with his wisdom and feeling.

phrases.en: but once it gets expressed, in speech
which is like when G-d said, "Let there be light"

phrases.he: הוא מהות דבר נבדל בפני עצמו,
phrases.en: then it becomes something separate

phrases.he: והוא בחינת חכמה שבחסד דמלכות שנמשך מבחינת מלכות דחכממה דחסד שבזעיר אנפין
phrases.en: and these come from the *Malchus* of *chachma* of *chesed* of *Zeir Anpin*, right?
each thing comes from its specific source

blocks.text: Once it is expressed in speech, as when G-d said "let there be light," it becomes a separate thing.

blocks.title: A parent's good intention
blocks.text: Take a parent, or Moshe, who has the best intentions and then writes down or says what should be done. The words may not be understood with the depth and perspective of the one who first said them.

blocks.title: When the father reads
blocks.text: Like the *Hayom Yom*: the Mitteler Rebbe always heard his father, the Alter Rebbe, read the rebuke. When the Alter Rebbe was away and someone else read it, he got very sick. Asked why, since he hears it every year, he said, "When Father reads, I don't hear curses." The Rebbe points out that the verse says "when a father reads," not "my father": it is read with the fatherly love of *chesed*. Read without that, it is harsh, cruel judgment.
The other aspect: G-d can create something that is still attached to Him. *Malchus* is when He makes it feel completely separate.

When G-d said "let there be light," His *chachma* of *chesed* became a physical thing, and also spiritual things: the understanding that grasps the light of Torah, and physical light. So this essential *chachma* of *chesed* seems separate from Him.

blocks.title: An author and his book
blocks.text: This is like an author who imagines a world, then writes a book or makes a film. The audience gets what it gets: maybe it understands right, maybe not. Like this book: the Mitteler Rebbe put his wisdom into it, and now we try to extract it.
All these chapters are related to each other, as in the *reshimu*.

blocks.title: Hidden light
blocks.text: Similarly, the idea is put into letters and becomes separate, with the light hidden inside, which we must extract. It can be hidden from us, though the giver sees it.

So the *chachma* of *chesed* seems to be a separate thing: our sense of what is logical and intuitive, what is right and wrong, which G-d puts into our soul; and the light, not only physical light but all experiences of consciousness. These are the *chachma* of *chesed* of *Malchus*.
These come from *Zeir Anpin*: G-d chose to create this experience and then chose to separate it, so each thing comes from its specific source.

phrases.he: וכך הוא כל בנין פרטים דעשר ספירות דמלכות באורות וכלים בפרצוף בפני עצמו כו'
phrases.en: and so too with all of the details of the ten *sefiros* of *Malchus*, with the lights and the vessels, it becomes its own *partzuf*

blocks.text: The same is true of all the details of the ten *sefiros* of *Malchus*: lights and vessels, a face of its own.
*Malchus* relates to many things, such as the Written Torah and the Oral Torah.
It relates to going from the *Ein Sof* to the finite, creating time and place.
It relates to *Knesses Yisrael*, to souls that seem separate, and to angels. The soul is like *Zeir Anpin* relative to the body, which is like *Malchus*.
It is also the idea, in a less essential way, that something revealed as limited is the whole concept of *gvul*, nature, *teva* and all these kinds of things.
There seems to be a reality on each of these levels: separate beings, a separate world, a nature and logic that seem separate. That is what goes on with *Malchus* becoming its own face.
It is really all G-d's choice: He creates and invents all this, and it does not have to exist this way at all. But we lose that sense.

sections.title: Before the separation, Malchus is the back that follows the face
sections.summary: Kabbalah reads the Midrash this way: before the separation, Malchus is the back that follows the face, without an essence of its own. Afterward it is built into its own partzuf.

phrases.en: before the separation, before *Malchus* was separated from *Zeir Anpin*, there were two *partzufim*

phrases.he: ד"ו פרצופין, שכמו האחוריים שנגרר אחר הפנים,
phrases.en: like the back that's automatically drawn after the face
without its own nature

blocks.text: Before the separation there were two faces, like the back that follows the face. This is how Kabbalah sees it, based on the *Midrashim*: *Malchus* was attached to the back of *Zeir Anpin* without an essence of its own.

phrases.he: כך בבחינת אחוריים דכל ספירה היה נכלל בחינת התגלות דמלכות,
phrases.en: and so the revelation of *Malchus* was just connected to every *sefira* as its lowest thing
that if you have 200, you automatically have 100

blocks.text: In each *sefira* the back includes the revelation of *Malchus* as its lowest part: if you have 200, you automatically have 100.

blocks.title: The author's draft
blocks.text: Think of an author in the creative process: the final product exists only as the expression of his creativity, until it is formed and becomes its own separate thing.

phrases.he: (וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בפרטים ענין אחור באחור ואחור בפנים כו'
phrases.en: and elsewhere it explains the different stages of this
or the opinion that says that it was a tail

blocks.text: Elsewhere the stages are explained: back to back, then front to back, or the opinion that it was a tail. These are the different relationships of *Malchus* to *Zeir Anpin*.

phrases.en: so *Malchus* starts out as just one point, one little dot, which is a *nekudah* under the *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin*
like it says, that Esther threw herself to the feet of

until it becomes a *heh* like it originally was

blocks.text: This is the general idea: *Malchus* goes from being attached to *Zeir Anpin* to being its own thing.
Its building goes through stages like those of *Zeir Anpin*, from undeveloped to mature. *Malchus* is built up step by step.

*Malchus* starts out as just one point, a *nekudah* under the *yesod* of *Zeir Anpin*, as Esther threw herself at the feet of Achashverosh. That is the level where *Malchus* makes herself like a *nekudah*.

blocks.title: Clay and language
blocks.text: Our relationship starts with simple acceptance of the yoke. Like clay that can be stamped, a medium must be refined enough to take a form; a language needs the flexibility and vocabulary to express thoughts in it.
This is like the three stages explained before, of thought, speech and action: first a person has experiences, then they become sounds, then they are strung together into words.
*Nekudah*. The Zohar's *osei devaro*: the simple meaning is that we do Hashem's words, or that angels and the things of the world do them. There is also the idea that we make His words.
*Binyan hamalchus*. It says *azei'ras gramah kenekudah*: first *Malchus* makes itself small like a point, totally *bittul*. That is the idea of *kabbalas ol*.
It is built back up until it is a *heh* again, as it originally was: it starts as a point and is built up to a full face.

phrases.he: שאחר כך נבנית בפרצוף בבחינת האצילות
phrases.en: and then *Malchus* becomes a full *partzuf*

phrases.he: עד שנעשית בבחינת פנים בפנים כו'
phrases.en: until it becomes face to face, becomes like an equal to *Zeir Anpin*

blocks.text: Then *Malchus* is built into a full *partzuf* within *Atzilus*, face to face with *Zeir Anpin*, like partners, as a husband and wife.

phrases.en: and this is similar, compared to the moon
you see the fullness of the moon

blocks.title: The moon, new and full
blocks.text: The sun is *Zeir Anpin* and the moon is *Malchus*. When the moon is very close to the sun, you see only its dark side, the new moon. As it moves away and faces the sun, you see the full moon. That represents us as receivers: the full awareness of G-dliness comes afterwards, but it is based first on *bittul*.

blocks.title: Learning a language or an instrument
blocks.text: It is the same with learning anything: first *bittul*, readiness to do what is required and to practice; then comes mastery, and you can express yourself in that medium.
Likewise, to see G-dliness in the world we first need *bittul*: the yoke of heaven, and Torah and *mitzvos*. Then our view of the world is transformed.
The same is true of the body, the animal soul and the evil inclination. They seem to cover G-dliness, but mastered, they can be built up into something good.

He recently saw teachings of the *Baal Shem Tov* on this: why, after listing the differences between the students of Abraham and of Balaam, does the verse add, "and what is the difference between them?" The difference is in the traits, humility against pride and contentment against wanting wealth, and each side can have either. A proud student of Abraham says, "I must do extra mitzvos, since I am important"; a humble student of Balaam says, "Who am I to do a mitzva?" and uses it in a bad way.
A person who follows the path of *chachma* turns even these traits of the animal soul and the evil inclination into something good. Refining ourselves is part of our *avoda*.

He thinks this is also an aspect: serving from the G-dly soul is like *Zeir Anpin*, natural love and feeling. Training the animal soul through Torah and mitzvos, and understanding G-dliness within human reason, refines it until it too is a *kli* for G-dliness.
That is also part of this: the waning of the moon.

phrases.en: and this is the main idea of the building of

phrases.he: שהוא למעלה מבנין המלכות בפרצוף בבי"ע,
phrases.en: we're talking about the higher aspect of it, which is building it within
that it can actually be something within holiness just like equal to

phrases.he: עד בחינת מלכות דמלכות שבוקע המסך ונעשית בבחינת פרצוף בבריאה,
phrases.en: completely hidden until just the lowest part of it
we're going to talk more about that later

blocks.text: The building of *Malchus* has two aspects: within *Atzilus*, and as a source for the lower worlds.

The higher aspect is building it within itself, so it can be holy and equal to *Zeir Anpin*. *Malchus* can be hidden until only its lowest part breaks through the screen and becomes a separate face in *Beriya*.

This is explained later. Within *Atzilus* itself, *Malchus* can be built up to be holy: the Oral Torah can equal the Written Torah, and the soul can become holy. The *chesed* of *Atzilus* was jealous of Avraham's *chesed*; our service through the body can equal service through the soul.
Seeing G-d in nature is an equal revelation to seeing Him as infinite.

blocks.title: A factory that runs by itself
blocks.text: The *Rebbe* gives an example he thinks relates: a factory that runs by itself, with no one there. The creator put his wisdom into every detail, so present that he need not be there, like a child who becomes independent because we give our whole essence there.
Looking at nature, we see G-dliness revealed within it; that too is a revelation of G-dliness. He thinks these are all different aspects of this idea.

sections.title: Malchus as greatness in Atzilus, and speech before it is spoken
sections.summary: In Atzilus, the Nukva of Zeir Anpin is in its full greatness, with mochin, middos, lights and vessels, and it is called large because it is at its source. Malchus is the keser of Malchus of Atzilus: the power of speech before it spreads into speech.

שהוא בחינת גדלות פרצוף נוקבא דזעיר אנפין בבחינת האצילות,
phrases.en: this is the state of maturity, of the *partzuf* of *Nukva* of *Zeir Anpin*, when it's still within *Atzilus*
when it's completely mature, and that's why it's called large, because it's at its source

and so first *Malchus* was built up on the level of *Atzilus*, and then it goes down

blocks.title: Opening: the ideas of Malchus at every level
blocks.text: Malchus is not only an analogy: the same idea is on every level of the descent from the top down. The *Ein Sof* is expressed in our *yechida*, and Malchus is expressed in the body: it feels separate from the soul, which controls it but is limited by it, and sometimes fights us to do what we want.
blocks.outOfPlace: The class opens with a review of Malchus before it reads line 26.

blocks.text: The same is true of the outside world and of creations, and of Torah and mitzvos done with *kabbalas ol*, or because we have to, while feeling separate from Him.
blocks.outOfPlace: The class opens with a review of Malchus before it reads line 26.

blocks.text: But *Malchus* is also an expression of inherent G-dliness: our G-dly soul is revealed, and G-d's power of limitation reveals Him, so we can see these things as a revelation of G-dliness.
blocks.outOfPlace: The class opens with a review of Malchus before it reads line 26.

blocks.text: These are all different aspects of this idea, something to keep in mind as the chapter goes on.
blocks.outOfPlace: The class opens with a review of Malchus before it reads line 26.

blocks.text: This is the idea of the large *dalet* of *Echad*: *Malchus* is still within *Atzilus*, a revelation of the sefiros in us in our service. Our G-dly soul is a revelation of our essence (*etzem*), and this is the building of *Malchus* we do in the Ten Days of Teshuvah. It is also seeing the outside world as a revelation of Hashem: "G-d is everything, everything is G-d." There are two aspects of seeing G-dliness in everything.
blocks.outOfPlace: The class opens with a review of Malchus before it reads line 26.

blocks.text: This is the state of *gadlus*: the *partzuf* of *Nukva* in *Atzilus*, with *mochin*, *middos*, lights and vessels, large because it is at its source.

There is a unique, full, rich expression of G-dliness in the *koach hagvul* and in nature. We see G-dliness through miracles above nature, and also in nature, limitation and the creatures. You can see G-dliness in our G-dly soul, even in our body.
Like it says, *vayiven Hashem Elokim et ha-tzela*, and this is similar to how the Oral Torah is called *Malchus*: built up into a whole, rich thing that conveys.
Hashem built the side into Chava, making her her own complete face, equal to Adam. *Abba* and *Ima*, *chachma* and *bina* of *Atzilus*, built up *Malchus* and told her, "go guard your house."
So *Malchus* was first built up on the level of *Atzilus*, and then it goes down: a mother is both a wife to her husband and a mother to the children. There are two levels of relationship.

phrases.en: as it's known about the idea that it says the well was dug by the princes

blocks.text: It says the well was dug by the princes, Moshe and Aharon, and they dug Miriam's well.

phrases.he: והענין הוא דבחינת דבור שבמחשבה הנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: this is the idea that you have a *dibur* of *machshava*

phrases.en: and this is the idea that the word of the king rules

phrases.en: and so the *keser* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus* is this *koach* of *dibur*

phrases.he: בבחינת שכל ומדות שבדבור, שהוא ט׳ ספירות דמלכות
phrases.en: and the actual process of speaking, of figuring out what to say, that's the

blocks.text: This is the *dibur* of *machshava*, the *dalet rabbasi*, made into the upper *dibur* of *Zeir Anpin*: ten *sefiros*, lights and vessels.

A person thinking to himself rehearses what he will say; this goes back to the potential idea before the *tzimtzum*. First you think of yourself and what you want to express, and how to reveal it to another. So *dibur* begins as self-expression.

From this deeper G-dliness Hashem creates the world to reveal Himself: the logic of Torah and mitzvos, the neshamos, the malachim, the physical world and the body. From one perspective it is an expression of G-dliness, the real purpose; from our perspective it is the *dibur* itself.
*Malchus* of each of the nine sefiros of *Zeir Anpin* is the source of *Malchus* itself.
This is the *kavana* of *Echad*: the nine *sefiros*, *alef* and *chet*, go into the *dalet*, into *Malchus*, as explained elsewhere at length.
Like it says that man became a living soul: the Onkelos translation of *nefesh chaya* is a speaking soul.
The word of the king rules, with the ten *ma'amarot* by which Hashem created the world, like "let there be light." So first there is this beginning.
Because He is infinite, Hashem also has the power of limitation, to reveal G-dliness to us; from our perspective it seems separate.
The *keser* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus* is this *koach* of *dibur*, before it spreads into speech: Hashem already has the power to create what will feel separate.

blocks.title: An author and the reader
blocks.text: Like an author who wants to create a certain experience for the reader: he knows what he conveys, and sees it from the audience's perspective.
Hashem already has the power to create something from nothing that will feel separate. Working out what to say is the *sechel* and *middos* of *dibur*, the nine *sefiros* of *Malchus*.

sections.title: Malchus is dal: it has nothing of its own but what Zeir Anpin gives
sections.summary: Malchus is called dal (poor). It has nothing on its own, and receives all it has from Zeir Anpin, as the moon receives from the sun. Its building comes from chesed, and like learning a language, the words are dead until meaning is put into them.

phrases.he: והיינו ענין לעולם יהו״ה דברך נצב
phrases.en: that the words of *Hashem* are always standing in the heavens
what does it mean standing in

phrases.he: דהיינו בחינת כח הדבור שדבוק בחזה דזעיר אנפין תמיד כו',
phrases.en: so, in other words, the source of *dibur* is always connected to *Zeir Anpin*

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב בעץ חיים ומבואר במקום אחר
phrases.en: like it says in *Etz Chaim*, it's explained elsewhere

blocks.text: The words of Hashem are always standing in the heavens, as the Tanya quotes from the *Baal Shem Tov*. Heaven is *Zeir Anpin*, so the source of *dibur* is always connected to *Zeir Anpin*.
This is the power of speech, always connected to the *chazeh* (chest) of *Zeir Anpin*. A person speaks only if he is in a good mood, and he needs both something to say and the motivation to say it.
Look at creation: things seem independent, but where does their nature come from? Trees want to grow, things want to fall, like gravity. Where does that will come from?

Ultimately it comes from the choices Hashem makes in how He conducts the world, from *Zeir Anpin*. So it always has to stay connected, or it would go back to nothing. This is also in *Etz Chaim*, explained elsewhere.

phrases.he: והתפשטות המלכות מלבשת לתנה"י דזעיר אנפין, שהוא בחינת דלי"ת,
phrases.en: and another aspect of this *dalet* is the fact that
but *Malchus* itself is called poor

blocks.text: *Malchus* covers over, or expresses, the four lower *sefiros* of *Zeir Anpin*: that is another idea of four. There are levels of this idea of the *dalet*, of how *Malchus* is connected to its source.
*Malchus* itself is called *dal* (poor): totally *bittul*, with nothing. That is why it is called a *dalet*.

phrases.he: ושרש בנין המלכות מחסדים דזעיר אנפין,
phrases.en: and the source of *Malchus* being built up
like it says, Hashem founded His throne with kindness
happy, fortunate is the one that thinks about the poor
which means to have pity

phrases.he: דהמלכות לית לה מגרמה כלום, רק מה שמקבלת מזעיר אנפין
phrases.en: because *Malchus* has nothing on its own, only what it receives from *Zeir Anpin*

blocks.text: The source of *Malchus* being built up is the *chesed* of *Zeir Anpin*: accepting Hashem as king with simple *kabbalas ol*, the level of *dal*, having nothing of one's own.

Then the *chesed* of *Zeir Anpin* is the acceptance of the *mitzvos*. Through understanding, *ahava* and *yirah*, and through *bittul*, we become a *kli* to reveal our *neshama*. Like it says, Hashem founded His throne with kindness, and happy is the one who thinks about the poor.

This is how it works on each level: the body and the neshama, and Torah and mitzvos from *kabbalas ol*, into which Hashem puts understanding and reasons so they carry meaning and inspiration. Like learning a language: the words are dead at first, and you put meaning and feeling into them. That is the *chesed* of *Zeir Anpin* going into them.
The word *chesed* is *chas* and *dalet*: *chas* means to have pity, and *dalet* is *Malchus*, which has nothing except what it receives from *Zeir Anpin*.

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל בענין התגלות דהתגלות כו',
phrases.en: that this is the idea of a revelation for a revelation
and this is like the moon that receives from the light of the sun

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב בזהר דסיהרא לית לה מגרמה כו'

blocks.text: This is a *revelation for a revelation*, like what is engraved into a ring and then stamped into something else. As explained before, it goes back to the engraving of letters.

blocks.title: The moon that receives
blocks.text: Like the moon, which receives the light of the sun and reflects it to us.
The word is spelled as a door (*delet*), not with a *dalet*. People just say *dal*, the way they contract words.
So the *neshama* can be codified, as the Oral Torah is, but it all comes from a higher perspective, still wholly connected to that revelation.

sections.title: Two levels of Malchus: in Atzilus, and as the head of the lower worlds
sections.summary: Malchus has two levels: its place in Atzilus, and its descent to become the head of the lower worlds, where it is hidden like the night. The class then turns to how the same descent feels in a person's service.

phrases.he: אך יש ב' מדריגות גם בבנין הנוקבא, הא' בבחינת האצילות שהוא ענין הנסירה כו',

phrases.en: and the second, where it becomes the head for

blocks.text: The second level is the head of the lower worlds: you use what you have to train an immature person to follow the *Shulchan Aruch*, without the depth behind it.
Is it like *tzimtzum*, or even the same idea? From the giver's view, seeing the *Mishnah*, he sees the whole *Gemara* in his notes. The receiver sees it small, but can grow and extract the whole.

phrases.he: (והוא מה שכתוב במקום אחר בענין לכי ומעטי את עצמך כו',
phrases.en: go and make yourself small, and go down into

phrases.he: שזהו בחינת המלכות שנעשית ראש לשועלים בבי"ע,
phrases.en: from being the tail of the lion to becoming the head of the foxes

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב ואת המאור הקטן לממשלת הלילה
phrases.en: that once Hashem made the moon small, He set it to be in the night time, to be the ruler of the night

blocks.text: This is the *go and make yourself small*: Hashem tells *Malchus* to go down into the lower worlds, from the tail of the lion to the head of the foxes, as is explained elsewhere.
As it says, the smaller light was made small and set to rule the night. Night is where things are, and G-dliness is hidden.

phrases.he: ובכלל כל בחינת האצילות נקרא יום,
phrases.en: and in general the whole light of *Atzilus* is called a day

phrases.he: ומדת לילה הוא בחינת המלכות כשמסתתרת בראש הבריאה, כמו שיתבאר בסמוך בענין ברוך שם כבוד מלכותו לעולם ועד כו',
phrases.en: and the *middah* of night is when *Malchus* gets hidden, limited, and hidden, and goes to become the head of

phrases.he: אחר בקיעת המסך כו' ודי למבין)
phrases.en: and it's enough to understand

blocks.text: In general, the whole light of *Atzilus* is called a day.
*Malchus* becomes the head of the lower worlds when it is hidden and limited: the *middah* of night. He will explain this soon, after the *masach* (screen).
Torah and mitzvos can be seen as expressions of G-dliness, or from an immature view: "I don't really want to, but I have to," with *kabbalas ol*, which eventually trains me.
The difference: serving from the G-dly soul, where *hisbonenus* fills what is revealed; serving from the natural soul, where one understands logically why to serve.
So in general there is service from the soul and service from the body, which comes with some *yeshus* and is missing something to a degree. There are also *tzadikim* and *beinonim*.
In the lower worlds the soul feels separate and independent, with its own free choice; that is how *Malchus* comes down. There I feel I can serve Hashem or go against Him.
Even when I do the right thing in the lower worlds, my *bittul* comes with some selfhood, because I chose it.
In *Atzilus* the soul feels it is a G-dly thing, so it is compelled, because that is who it is. As in: "What do you mean, I'm a Jew? Of course I have to do it."
That is the difference between a person's feeling in *Atzilus* and in the lower worlds, where it is revealed in a smaller, more hidden way.

reviewQuestions.question: What is Malchus, and why is it called the world of speech?
How does Malchus separate from Zeir Anpin, and what is that like in Adam and Chava?
Why does speech turn a feeling into a yesh of its own?
What are the tzelem and the demus, and how do they differ?
How is Malchus built from a single point into a full face?
What does it mean that Malchus is dal, and that it is the head of the lower worlds?
